module_title: Union Territory & Citizenship - Constitutional Cases, CAA, and Overseas Citizens
introduction: This advanced level explores the Supreme Court rulings regarding ceding Indian territory to foreign nations, the nuances of the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), and the distinctions between NRIs, PIOs, and OCIs.

core_concepts.title: Berubari Union Case (1960)
core_concepts.description: The Supreme Court ruled that the power of Parliament to diminish the area of a state (under Article 3) does NOT cover the cession (giving away) of Indian territory to a foreign country. Ceding territory requires a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368. (This led to the 9th CAA, 1960).

core_concepts.title: 100th Constitutional Amendment Act (2015)
core_concepts.description: Enacted to give effect to the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh. India transferred 111 enclaves to Bangladesh and received 51 enclaves in return, validating the Berubari ruling that land exchange requires a CAA.

core_concepts.title: Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019
core_concepts.description: Amended the 1955 Act to grant citizenship to persecuted religious minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India on or before December 31, 2014. It notably excluded Muslims from these three countries.

core_concepts.title: Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)
core_concepts.description: Introduced in 2005 (merging the PIO card scheme later in 2015). An OCI cardholder gets a multi-purpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa to visit India. However, they do NOT have voting rights, cannot hold constitutional posts, and cannot buy agricultural land.

core_concepts.title: Exceptions to Article 15 & 16 based on Citizenship
core_concepts.description: Fundamental Rights available ONLY to citizens (and denied to aliens) are Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30. All other Fundamental Rights (like Art 14, 21) are available to both citizens and foreigners.

important_entities.name: L.M. Singhvi Committee
important_entities.significance: Constituted in 2000, this committee recommended the amendment of the Citizenship Act to provide for the grant of dual citizenship (in the form of OCI) to Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs).

important_entities.name: Sikkim's Integration (1975)
important_entities.significance: Sikkim was an independent protectorate. The 35th CAA made it an 'Associate State' (creating a unique Article 2A). A year later, the 36th CAA made it a full-fledged State of the Indian Union, repealing Article 2A.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While ceding territory to a foreign state requires a Constitutional Amendment (Article 368), the Supreme Court ruled in 1969 that the *settlement of a boundary dispute* does NOT require an amendment. It can be done by executive action (as it doesn't involve giving away confirmed Indian territory).

UPSC and PCS exams often set a trap stating India offers dual citizenship to diaspora. The Constitution strictly forbids dual citizenship (Article 9). OCI is a residency status with specific benefits, not actual citizenship.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorize these five numbers. They represent rights against discrimination (15), public employment (16), freedoms (19), and cultural/educational rights (29, 30) exclusively for citizens.

exam_strategy_tips: In statements regarding the CAA 2019, look closely at the cut-off date (Dec 31, 2014) and the specific 3 countries and 6 religions mentioned.
Assertion-Reasoning questions frequently use the Berubari Union case to test your understanding of the limits of Article 3 versus Article 368.
